title: Wire observability-pack install into Private installer (pinning + rollback safety)
author: Bruno Silva
release_notes:
- Private installer can now install/upgrade the "observability minimum pack" bundle (dashboards + Prometheus rules + logging defaults) in a version-pinned way.
- Installer persists installed pack version and supports automatic rollback on failure.
body:
Context: As part of the “Private observability minimum pack” workstream, we need the Private installer to handle installing a versioned observability bundle (Grafana dashboards provisioning, PrometheusRule groups, and log pipeline defaults) without bespoke customer steps. This PR wires the observability-pack lifecycle into the installer with: (1) explicit version pinning, (2) integrity checks, (3) idempotent apply, and (4) rollback safety to avoid leaving clusters with half-applied rules/dashboards.

What this PR does: Adds a new installer step `observability_pack` to the standard install/upgrade flow. The step downloads the pack artifact for a pinned version (defaults to the installer’s embedded compatibility matrix), verifies a SHA256 checksum, and applies resources in a deterministic order: namespace + RBAC, then Prometheus rules, then Grafana provisioning (folders/dashboards + datasource refs), then logging ConfigMaps (forwarder defaults). The installer persists the installed pack version and artifact digest in a cluster-scoped ConfigMap (`redwood-private/observability-pack-state`) to make upgrades/rollbacks explicit and auditable.

Versioning and pinning: Introduces `--observability-pack-version` (and `installer.yaml: observability.packVersion`) with a default derived from a small compatibility map keyed by installer version. If the customer pins a version explicitly, we skip auto-selection and treat the pin as authoritative (but still validate it exists). Pack artifacts are resolved via `--observability-pack-source` (default: `redwood`), where `redwood` means “download from the Redwood release artifact base URL” (configurable for Private environments that mirror artifacts internally). Air-gapped/local bundle support is not included here (handled in follow-up PR #909), but this PR structures the code so a `file://` source can be plugged in cleanly.

Rollback safety: We’ve seen upgrades fail due to PrometheusRule parsing / RBAC / Grafana provisioning ordering (see SUP-2431, INT-1184). This PR adds a conservative rollback mechanism: before applying a new pack version, we snapshot the previous pack manifests as last-known-good (stored as a gzipped manifest blob in the state ConfigMap, capped in size with clear error messaging). If apply fails at any stage, we attempt to re-apply the previous manifest set and restore the state ConfigMap. The rollback is best-effort and logs every action; if rollback also fails, the installer exits non-zero with remediation guidance.

Security considerations: Downloads are checksum-verified (SHA256). We do not embed credentials in dashboards or provisioning resources. The installer uses the existing least-privilege service account model and only needs additional permissions for the specific resources we apply (ConfigMaps, Secrets references, PrometheusRule CRDs, and Grafana provisioning ConfigMaps). No cluster-admin requirement is introduced beyond what the installer already uses for Private core components.

Operator UX: The installer prints a concise summary at the end of install/upgrade: selected pack version, artifact digest, apply status by phase, and pointers to validation commands (the richer post-install validation command lands in PR #908). Failures include actionable hints (e.g., PrometheusRule CRD missing, Grafana API unreachable, RBAC denies) and link to the runbook section names used by Docs.

Testing: Added unit tests for version selection, source resolution, checksum verification, state ConfigMap roundtrips, and rollback paths. Added a lightweight Kind-based integration test that installs a dummy pack, then upgrades to a pack with an intentionally invalid PrometheusRule to validate rollback restores the prior working state. CI runs `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint`, and the Kind smoke test.

Follow-ups: (1) PR #908 adds the post-install validation command that checks rule loading / Grafana reachability / required endpoints. (2) PR #909 adds air-gapped/local bundle support and docs updates. (3) Observability-pack repo PRs provide the pack artifacts that this installer expects (folder layout + manifest schema).
commits: installer: add observability pack step skeleton + wiring into install/upgrade pipeline
installer/observability: implement artifact resolver (version pinning + base URL override)
installer/observability: checksum verification + streaming download with temp dir hygiene
installer/observability: apply phases + deterministic ordering + improved error surfaces
installer/observability: persist pack state (version + digest + last-known-good snapshot)
tests: unit coverage for resolver/state/rollback + kind integration for rollback path
changed_files: pkg/installer/steps/observability_pack.go (main lifecycle: resolve, verify, apply, rollback)
pkg/observabilitypack/apply.go (phase apply helpers + kubectl/server-side apply wrapper)
review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Rollback semantics look good, but can we guarantee we don’t page on transient rule load during upgrade? Also, what happens if PrometheusRule CRD isn’t installed yet?
Bruno Silva (author): For now we apply rules after verifying the CRD exists; if missing, we fail early with a clear message and do not touch existing state. On transient rule load: we apply rule groups last-known-good first, then apply new rules; if the new rules fail, we rollback immediately. We’re not managing alert inhibition here, but the window is bounded to the apply step duration and we’re avoiding partial rule groups by applying per-file and checking server responses.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Ack. Please add a note in the failure output to confirm CRD requirement and point to the runbook section name.
Bruno Silva (author): Added: error now includes “Prereq: Prometheus Operator / PrometheusRule CRD must be installed” and references Day-2 runbook section label `Missing CRDs`.

Marcus Lin (Security): We should not accept unsigned artifacts. Checksum is better than nothing, but can we at least pin the expected digest in config to avoid TOCTOU on the download endpoint?
Bruno Silva (author): Agreed on signatures long-term; in this PR we add checksum verification where the checksum is fetched from the same release bucket. I can also support an override `observability.packSha256` so customers can pin digest out-of-band.
Marcus Lin (Security): Yes, add `packSha256` override and require it when `--observability-pack-source` is not `redwood`.
Bruno Silva (author): Implemented: optional `packSha256` can be specified; when source is `custom`/non-redwood, digest becomes required (installer errors if absent).

Fatima Noor (On-prem/air-gapped): This assumes network egress to fetch artifacts. Can we avoid hard-coding the URL and make it clear that an internal mirror is supported?
Bruno Silva (author): Yes; added `--observability-pack-artifact-base-url` / `installer.yaml: observability.artifactBaseURL`. Air-gapped local path is coming in #909, but mirroring to an internal HTTP endpoint will work with this PR.
Fatima Noor (On-prem/air-gapped): Please ensure temp files are cleaned up and no leftover tarballs remain on disk in failure paths.
Bruno Silva (author): Added `defer os.RemoveAll(tmpDir)` and a cleanup block that runs on both success and failure; tests updated to assert cleanup on error.

Sergio Costa (Dashboards/alerts): Can you confirm expected pack layout? I want to make sure the installer applies files in a stable order so dashboard provisioning is deterministic.
Bruno Silva (author): Installer expects tarball root: `manifests/` (k8s yaml), `grafana/` (provisioning files), `logging/` (forwarder configs). Apply order is explicit and stable, and within a directory we sort filenames lexicographically before apply.
Sergio Costa (Dashboards/alerts): Great. Please add a log line that prints the resolved pack version and digest before apply; it helps debugging.
Bruno Silva (author): Added at step start and end.

Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Any impact on upgrade time? Also we should document the compatibility map location because backports will need updates.
Bruno Silva (author): Adds ~3–10s depending on artifact size/network; apply time dominates. Compatibility map lives in `pkg/observabilitypack/compat.go` with a comment on backport policy. I also added a CI check to ensure the current installer version exists in the map (fails fast in PRs).
